title: Ian Paice - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 111,991. Ian Anderson Paice, born 29 June 1948, Nottingham; early years in Germany, then Bicester near Oxford; his father a civil servant; first kit at 15, played in his father's dance band; Georgie and the Rave-Ons (later the Shindigs), then the Maze (originally MI5), from 1966; Deep Purple from March 1968, the only member in every line-up and on every album; Paice Ashton Lord (1976-1978), Whitesnake (1979-1982), Gary Moore (1982-1984); the Velvet Underground's Squeeze (1973), George Harrison (1989), Paul McCartney's Run Devil Run (1999); 'primarily left-handed', plays a left-handed kit with matched grip; 'extremely fast and smooth single and double-stroke rolls'; Ludwig in the 1970s and early 1980s, large sizes, a 14 x 6.5 Supraphonic snare; Pearl from 1982, Paiste, Remo, Pro-Mark; prefers one bass drum; influences Gene Krupa, Buddy Rich, Bobby Elliott, Ringo Starr, Charles Connor, later Carmine Appice, Ginger Baker, Mitch Mitchell; influenced Clive Burr, Mikkey Dee, Virgil Donati, Dave Grohl, Gary James, Simon Phillips, Matt Starr; Blackmore: 'He's an incredible drummer. And he was the motor of the band.'; a transient ischaemic attack on 14 June 2016; Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Deep Purple, 8 April 2016.

title: Ken Micallef, 'Deep Purple's Ian Paice', Modern Drummer, 1 September 2020
notes: 'I'm playing big band music in a rock 'n' roll context. That inherent swing and feel harkens back to those days.' 'My bass drum is on the beat, or maybe even slightly ahead, but my backbeat—the snare drum—is behind it.' On rimshots: 'A rimshot on the snare makes things obvious, especially when you're on a big stage', but 'sometimes you can play quieter in the middle of the head, which gives a much bigger impression'. 'I want the cymbals to ring.' 'I don't tune my bass drum for impact only.' On relaxing: he had been 'hitting harder than I should'. The kit listed: one bass drum on stage (14 x 26) and one in the studio (14 x 24); a steel snare, 'very rock 'n' roll, immensely powerful'.

title: Chris Welch, Ian Paice interview, Rhythm (c. late 1995), reprinted on The Highway Star
notes: No exact date; it refers to an album due in January 1996 and a March tour. 'Buddy Rich was a big influence on me; of all the big band drummers he stood out head and shoulders.' Influences 'mainstream and big band jazz'. 'If you can play singles right, everything else comes easy. Doubles are a doddle.' On Rich's single-stroke roll: 'I can do that roll at the same speed, but I can't keep it going anywhere near as long.' 'Go on threes.' 'All my knowledge of rudiments is self taught.' 'I don't like those mid-tempos where people stomp their feet.' Solos 'an easy way for the rest of the guys to go offstage and have a drink'. Loyal to Ludwig 'for a long time', then Pearl.

title: Lars-Oliver Horl, 'Die besten Drummer der Welt: Ian Paice (Deep Purple) – Die swingende Rockmaschine', Bonedo, 8 March 2026
notes: German. Left-handed on a mirrored kit; a one-handed snare roll (shown in a video with Chad Smith); taught himself fast single and double strokes; Black Night's 'shuffle groove'; a second bass drum on Fireball, otherwise one 26-inch bass drum; Burn's big fills; push and pull, the bass drum on or ahead of the beat and the backbeat behind; influences Gene Krupa, John Bonham, Carmine Appice (the 26-inch bass drum), Mitch Mitchell, Ginger Baker. Kits: a Ludwig Black Oyster Pearl four-piece early (22x14, 13x9, 16x16, 14x5 Supraphonic, later an 18x16 floor tom), Zildjian; a Ludwig Silver Sparkle of similar sizes from about 1971, used on Machine Head; Paiste from about 1971, the 2002 series his trademark; later a Ludwig with a 26x18 bass drum, 16x10, 18x16, 20x18, a 14x6.5 Supraphonic; Pearl from the 1980s. 'The only thing I can't handle is reggae.'

title: Paul Sexton, 'The Man Who Sets the Paice for Purple', uDiscover Music, 28 June 2014
notes: His first instrument the violin; to Melody Maker in 1971: 'I flogged the violin and found a tom-tom and some old biscuits tins.' A £32 kit, played along with his father, a pianist, in waltzes and quicksteps: 'a wee bit insipid, but it was a start'. International Times on the first album: Paice 'draws a line along the street which they all follow'.

title: Simon Poole, 'Speed King: Setting the Paice', in Who Do We Think They Are? Deep Purple and Metal Studies (Equinox, 2025), pp. 77-97
notes: Only the abstract and search summaries were read; the PDF on UAL Research Online could not be extracted here. Nine Mark II tracks examined; his virtuosity in intros, fills and trills without overshadowing the band; the double-kick intro of Fireball as a template for Simon Phillips on Judas Priest's Sin After Sin (1977) and Phil Taylor on Motorhead's Overkill (1979); credited with Bill Ward and John Bonham as a founder of the genre's rhythmic conventions; Rolling Stone placed him 21st.

title: 'Read and watch Lars Ulrich's passionate Deep Purple Rock Hall induction', deeppurple.com, 9 April 2016
notes: The speech of 8 April 2016: 'Behind him on the drums, little Ian Paice, a rock & roll cocktail of hair, sweat, spit and position', 'somehow, managing to wipe the steam off his glasses after he presses this great train forward'; 'every hard rock band in the last 40 years, including mine, traces its lineage directly back to Black Sabbath, Led Zeppelin and Deep Purple'.

title: Shades of Deep Purple - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded 11-13 May 1968, Pye Studios, ATV House, London; produced by Derek Lawrence; released 17 July 1968 (US, Tetragrammaton), September 1968 (UK, Parlophone). Rod Evans, Ritchie Blackmore, Nick Simper, Jon Lord, Ian Paice. Hush 4:24, No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100. Paice was 19, Evans's bandmate in the Maze; Blackmore knew him from Hamburg; chosen on the spot to replace Bobby Woodman.

title: Deep Purple in Rock - Wikipedia
notes: Released 5 June 1970 (UK); recorded October 1969 to April 1970 at IBC, De Lane Lea and Abbey Road; produced by Deep Purple. Gillan, Blackmore, Glover, Lord, Paice. Speed King 5:54; its UK intro ('Woffle') cut from the US album. Black Night released as a single on 5 June 1970, No. 2 in the UK, not on the album until the 25th-anniversary edition.

title: Fireball (Deep Purple song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded in London, March 1971. 'A rare instance of Ian Paice playing a double-bass drum'; often the encore live so the crew could add the second bass drum. The intro an air conditioner being switched on, recorded by Mike Thorne.

title: Machine Head (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 114,753. Released 30 March 1972 (UK, Purple); recorded 6-21 December 1971 at the Grand Hotel, Montreux, with the Rolling Stones Mobile; produced by Deep Purple, engineered by Martin Birch. Highway Star 6:05, Pictures of Home 5:03, Smoke on the Water 5:40, Lazy 7:19. On Fireball Paice had recorded his kit in a corridor because it sounded better; at the Grand Hotel the band set up at the end of a corridor. Pictures of Home's drum introduction was left off the original release and restored on the 25th-anniversary edition.

title: Burn (Deep Purple album) - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 118,035. Released 15 February 1974; recorded 8-14 November 1973 with the Rolling Stones Mobile in Montreux; produced by Deep Purple, engineered by Martin Birch. Blackmore, Coverdale, Hughes, Lord, Paice. Burn 6:00. His drumming 'strongly featured' on Burn; Lay Down, Stay Down his favourite on the album; You Fool No One grew from his drum pattern, which Hughes said was partly inspired by John Bonham.

title: Perfect Strangers (Deep Purple album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 29 October 1984; recorded 10 July to 26 August 1984 at Horizons, Stowe, Vermont, with Le Mobile; produced by Roger Glover and Deep Purple. The title track 5:31. Deborah Frost (Rolling Stone): 'Ian Paice's electrifying drumming'.

title: Deep Purple, 'Burn', California Jam, Ontario Motor Speedway, 6 April 1974 (ABC In Concert film), YouTube oxJT5PhP40k
notes: Frames read at 3:50 to 4:00: a Ludwig in Silver Sparkle, white coated heads, chrome; one rack tom, two floor toms on his left (the kit mirrored); round glasses, a yellow T-shirt, an open black waistcoat, curly shoulder-length hair.
